chapter_title: The Three Earths that Exist, they bear Fruit.
spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation

**¶1:** Three degrees of the human mind exist within the created order, and all are undergoing the labor of regeneration. At first they [GAP-1] the Divine working within them — resisting or only obscurely receiving the influx that would cultivate them. Afterward they bring forth [GAP-2: genuine goods of life] to the Divine purposes that labor within them.

**¶2:** The first of these is the natural mind, the outermost degree of consciousness in which human beings dwell. They break open its hardened states [GAP-3: with effort and persistence], prepare it with the rigid truths of external law and literal precepts, they order it, [GAP-4: forming] channels for the reception of interior truths, overturning its self-derived orientation [GAP-5: so that it faces toward what is above]. Afterward they gather the goods of life that spring from [GAP-6: this natural mind once it has been so reformed].

**¶3:** The second degree is the interior spiritual mind — the living rational soul, which is holy because it can receive the Divine directly. It is dispersed throughout every level of consciousness, both the higher and the lower. The Divine powers that labor upon it are Divine Love and Divine Wisdom, which proceed through the heavens in unceasing activity. They work upon the spiritual mind and cultivate it so as to draw whatever is good and true within it toward their own likeness. And that good, once freed, rises swiftly into elevated states of perception. It ascends out of every natural condition in which it had been imprisoned, and adds itself to the fullness of heaven.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: Three earths exist in the universe, and are being toiled over. At first they [weary] the farmer in them. Afterwards they bear [good] fruit to they who toil over them.

One of them is this great earth that people are living upon. They are ploughing in it [breaking], it with iron hoes, they cultivate, [making] the furrows, turning it over [to the light] Afterwards they harvest fruit from [it in its season]

The second field is the living soul, the holy one. It is mixed in the entire zone, above and below. The farmers who toil over it are these two great light-givers, which journey through the heavens. They are toiling and cultivating it, so that they will draw it towards their aspect. And it leaps up and comes to the heights. It goes upwards, out from every place wherein it is, and it adds to them.

fills.explanation: Uncultivated earth wearies the farmer before yielding fruit, corresponding to the natural mind resisting or only obscurely receiving the Divine influx that labors to regenerate it.
The editor's "good" correctly maps to the spiritual sense of "genuine goods of life" — good fruit is the standard agricultural expression for the produce of regenerated states.
The spiritual reading specifies "break open its hardened states," and "breaking it with iron hoes" is the natural agricultural action that parallels ploughing in a list of cultivation labors.
The editor's "making" fits well — "making the furrows" corresponds to "forming channels for the reception of interior truths," and is the standard agricultural expression for this action.

The spiritual sense is "so that it faces toward what is above" — in the Kephalaia's light-cosmology, turning the earth over "to the light" is the natural-plane equivalent of reorienting the natural mind toward the Divine, consistent with the chapter's later imagery of rising toward the heights.

The spiritual sense of "this natural mind once it has been so reformed" maps in agricultural register to the earth yielding fruit in its proper season — after the full cycle of cultivation has been completed.
